name: Shackleton Crater (South Pole)
coordinate_note: Per-site numbers were collected from published sources (LRO, Kaguya, Chandrayaan, Apollo, Luna, Chang'e, published papers) with source URLs. status=sourced means a URL exists; unverified means no published number was found (leave empty, do not estimate); weak_source means the only source is Wikipedia and should be replaced. Site coordinates are from IAU/USGS gazetteer or mission reports.

facts.unit: % of lunar year (near-continuous sun on high points)

facts.note: elevated hydrogen; LAMP UV albedo suggests surface frost in places
LRO LAMP far-UV albedo anomaly consistent with ~1-2% surface frost
no solar wind or micrometeorite flux in permanent shadow
crater walls block ~half of sky; GCR dose ~50% of surface
Shackleton rim is a NASA Artemis III candidate landing region
64 ppd (~474 m north-south grid); regional terrain, not landing hazards. Derivatives omitted above 85 degrees. Pixel spacing is not effective resolution; no uncertainty estimate supplied.
facts.method: Nearest native LDEM_64_FLOAT pixel; DN × 1000 m, relative to 1737.4 km sphere.
